title: Turkish coffee in the cezve
summary: In Turkey, coffee is made in a small long-handled copper pot called a cezve. Finely ground coffee, cold water and sugar are warmed slowly, often on hot sand, and the pot is lifted away each time the foam climbs, so the crown of foam survives and nothing boils over.
howToPlay: Read the order slip: it shows how many cups to make and how sweet each should be.
Tap the water jug, the coffee tin and the sugar bowl to fill the pot.
Slide the pot onto the glowing sand and lift it off as the foam reaches the green band. Repeat three times.
Lift the handle to tilt the pot and pour: foam first, then the coffee, in a thin stream down the side of each cup.
rules: The pot will not go on the sand until water and coffee are in it.
Foam that rises past the red line is a boil-over and earns nothing.
The pot must be lifted three times, each time as the foam reaches the green band.
A hard stream breaks the foam, so pour gently; cups should end level and nearly full.
Undo takes back the last ingredient added.
heritageNote: Brewing coffee in a copper cezve is an everyday craft across Turkey, passed from home to home and shared in cafes and kitchens. The skill lies in patience: slow heat, a well-timed lift and an even pour that gives every cup its share of foam.
